questions.prompt: Which of these is a program used on a client computer to view web pages?
questions.explanation: A browser (such as Chrome or Firefox) requests pages and shows them. A web server is the computer that stores and sends the pages.

questions.prompt: A collection of related web pages stored under one domain name is called a:
questions.explanation: A web page is a single document; a website is a set of linked web pages under one address.

questions.prompt: Sending a file from your computer to a computer on the Internet is called:
questions.explanation: Uploading sends a file to a remote computer; downloading brings a file from a remote computer to yours.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the Internet and the World Wide Web is correct?

expected_answer.value: The Web is a service that runs on the Internet

options: The Internet and the Web mean exactly the same thing
The Web is a service that runs on the Internet
The Internet runs on top of the Web
The Web is a type of web browser
questions.explanation: The Internet is the global network of networks. The World Wide Web is one service (linked pages) that uses it; email is another.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used to send email from a mail client to a mail server?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends outgoing mail. POP3 is used to fetch mail.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used to download your incoming email from a mail server to your device?
questions.explanation: POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) retrieves mail from the server. SMTP only sends.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between HTTP and HTTPS?

expected_answer.value: HTTPS encrypts the data sent between browser and server

options: HTTPS is faster because it skips the server
HTTP is used only for email
HTTPS encrypts the data sent between browser and server
HTTPS works only on mobile phones
questions.explanation: The S in HTTPS stands for Secure: data is encrypted, so others on the network cannot read it easily.

questions.prompt: In the TCP/IP pair of protocols, which job does TCP do?

expected_answer.value: Breaks data into packets and makes sure they arrive and are put back in order

options: Breaks data into packets and makes sure they arrive and are put back in order
questions.explanation: TCP handles reliable delivery of packets; IP handles addressing and routing them.

questions.prompt: Which tool lets you log in to a remote computer securely, with the session encrypted?
questions.explanation: SSH encrypts the whole session. TELNET also gives remote login but sends everything, including passwords, as plain text.

questions.prompt: Why is TELNET considered unsafe on open networks?

expected_answer.value: It sends data, including passwords, without encryption

options: It sends data, including passwords, without encryption
questions.explanation: Anyone watching the network could read what TELNET sends; SSH was designed to fix this.

questions.prompt: The protocol whose job is to move files between computers is:
questions.explanation: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) uploads and downloads files. SFTP and SCP do the same but securely.

questions.prompt: Which pair contains two SECURE ways to transfer files?
questions.explanation: SFTP and SCP both work over SSH, so the data is encrypted. Plain FTP and TELNET are not encrypted.

questions.prompt: A program that helps you find web pages by typing keywords is called a:
questions.explanation: Search engines such as Google or Bing look through an index of web pages and list matches.

questions.prompt: Paying an electricity bill through a mobile banking app is an example of:
questions.explanation: e-Banking means doing bank work (transfers, bills) over the Internet.

questions.prompt: Applying for a certificate on a government website instead of visiting the office is an example of:
questions.explanation: e-Governance uses the Internet to deliver government services to citizens.

questions.prompt: Attending a live class with several students at different places on one screen is an example of:
questions.explanation: Video conferencing lets people in different places see and hear each other in real time.

questions.prompt: What does SMS stand for?
questions.explanation: SMS carries short text messages between mobile phones.

questions.prompt: Which service can carry pictures, audio or video in a message, not only text?
questions.explanation: MMS (Multimedia Messaging Service) extends SMS to send media files.

questions.prompt: Compared with 4G, 5G mobile networks are designed to give:
questions.explanation: Each generation improved on the last; 5G aims for higher speed and lower latency than 4G.

questions.prompt: Which mobile technology first made video calling and mobile Internet practical for many phone users?
questions.explanation: 1G was analogue voice and 2G added digital calls and SMS. 3G brought mobile data fast enough for video calls and browsing.

questions.prompt: Which tag contains the text shown in the browser tab (title bar)?
questions.explanation: <title> sits inside <head>. Its text appears on the browser tab, not on the page itself.

questions.prompt: Which attribute of the <body> tag sets the background colour of the page?
questions.explanation: bgcolor sets the page colour. text sets the colour of normal text and link sets the colour of links.

questions.prompt: What does <body text="blue"> do?

expected_answer.value: Makes the normal text on the page blue

options: Makes the normal text on the page blue
Adds the word blue to the page
questions.explanation: The text attribute colours ordinary text. It does not change the background.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct basic order of a web page?
questions.explanation: <html> is the outer element; <head> comes first, then <body>.

questions.prompt: In <body background="sky.jpg">, what is sky.jpg used as?

expected_answer.value: A background picture for the page

options: A background picture for the page
questions.explanation: The background attribute takes the name of an image file to tile behind the page.

questions.prompt: Which tag inserts a line break?
questions.explanation:
breaks the line without starting a new paragraph.
draws a horizontal line.

questions.prompt: Which tag draws a horizontal line across the page?
questions.explanation: hr stands for horizontal rule.

questions.prompt: Which heading tag gives the LARGEST heading by default?
questions.explanation: <h1> is the biggest and <h6> the smallest heading.

questions.prompt: Which tag makes text italic?
questions.explanation: <i> italic, <b> bold, <u> underline.

questions.prompt: Which of these tags does NOT need a closing tag?
questions.explanation:
and
are empty tags: they have no content, so there is nothing to close.

questions.prompt: Which tag creates a bulleted (unordered) list?
questions.explanation: <ul> is unordered (bullets), <ol> is ordered (numbers). <li> is each item inside either list.

questions.prompt: What does <ol start="5"> do?
options: The list is hidden after item 5
questions.explanation: start sets the first number of an ordered list.

questions.prompt: Which code makes an ordered list with lowercase letters (a, b, c)?
questions.explanation: type="a" on <ol> gives a, b, c. Use type="A" for capital letters.

questions.prompt: In a description list, which tag holds the TERM being described?
questions.explanation: <dl> is the list, <dt> the term, <dd> its description.

questions.prompt: Which attribute changes the bullet style of an unordered list to squares?
questions.explanation: type on <ul> can be disc, circle or square.

questions.prompt: Which attribute of gives the file name or address of the picture?
questions.explanation: src (source) says where the image file is.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the alt attribute on an image?

expected_answer.value: Gives replacement text if the image cannot be shown, and helps screen readers

options: Links the image to another page
Gives replacement text if the image cannot be shown, and helps screen readers
questions.explanation: alt text is shown when the image fails to load and is read aloud for visually impaired users.

questions.prompt: Which pair of attributes sets the size of an image?
questions.explanation: width and height take values in pixels (or percent).

questions.prompt: Which tag is used to add a sound file to a page with play controls?
questions.explanation: <audio> embeds sound; the controls attribute shows play/pause buttons.

questions.prompt: Which tag embeds a video player in a web page?
questions.explanation: <video> (often with controls) is the HTML tag for video.

questions.prompt: Which tag defines a table row?
questions.explanation: tr = table row, td = data cell, th = header cell.

questions.prompt: Which tag creates a header cell that is bold and centred by default?
questions.explanation: <th> is a table header cell; <td> is an ordinary data cell.

questions.prompt: A cell that must stretch across 3 columns should use:
questions.explanation: colspan merges cells across columns; rowspan merges cells down rows.

questions.prompt: A cell that must stretch down 2 rows should use:
questions.explanation: rowspan merges cells vertically across rows.

questions.prompt: In a table written with 3 <tr> rows, each having 4 <td> cells and no merging, how many cells does the table show?
questions.explanation: 3 rows x 4 cells = 12 cells.

questions.prompt: Which input type hides what the user types, showing dots or stars instead?
questions.explanation: type="password" masks the characters.

questions.prompt: Which control should be used when the user may pick ONLY ONE option from a group?
questions.explanation: Radio buttons with the same name allow just one choice. Checkboxes allow several.

questions.prompt: Which control should be used when the user may tick MORE THAN ONE option, such as hobbies?
questions.explanation: Checkboxes are independent, so several can be ticked.

questions.prompt: For radio buttons to behave as one group, what must they share?
questions.explanation: Radio buttons with the same name belong to one group, so selecting one clears the others.

questions.prompt: Which tag with <option> items makes a drop-down list in a form?
questions.explanation: <select> holds <option> items and shows them as a drop-down list.

questions.prompt: Which attribute of <a> gives the address the link goes to?
questions.explanation: href (hypertext reference) holds the target address.

questions.prompt: Which link opens the visitor's email program to write to a given address?
questions.explanation: mailto: in the href starts a new email to that address.

questions.prompt: What does target="_blank" do on a link?

expected_answer.value: Opens the page in a new tab or window

options: Opens the page in a new tab or window
questions.explanation: _blank loads the destination in a new browsing context.

questions.prompt: In Click here, what does the visitor see on the page?

expected_answer.value: The words Click here as the link

options: The words Click here as the link
questions.explanation: The text between the opening and closing <a> tags is what is shown and clicked.

questions.prompt: What does CSS stand for?
questions.explanation: CSS describes how HTML elements look: colour, spacing, fonts and so on.

questions.prompt: Which CSS property sets the colour of text?
questions.explanation: color sets text colour; background sets the background.

questions.prompt: Which is a correct CSS rule?
questions.explanation: A rule has a selector, then braces, then property: value; pairs.

questions.prompt: Which CSS property puts empty space OUTSIDE the border of an element?
questions.explanation: margin is outside the border; padding is inside it.

questions.prompt: Which attribute lets you write CSS directly inside one HTML tag?
questions.explanation: style="color:blue;" applies CSS to just that element (inline style).

questions.prompt: Writing a whole message in CAPITAL LETTERS online is usually seen as:
options: A way to encrypt the message
questions.explanation: Netiquette asks us to keep a normal tone; capitals feel like shouting.

questions.prompt: Which is good netiquette in an online class chat?

expected_answer.value: Wait for your turn and write respectfully

options: Post the same message again and again
Wait for your turn and write respectfully
Share a classmate's photo without asking
questions.explanation: Respect, patience and privacy are the heart of netiquette.

questions.prompt: Sending unwanted bulk messages or advertisements to many people is called:
questions.explanation: Spam wastes people's time and can carry scams or malware.

questions.prompt: Before posting a group photo of your friends online, the best netiquette is to:
options: Post it, since you took the photo
Tag everyone so they cannot object
Delete it only if someone complains in court
questions.explanation: Photos show other people, so their consent and privacy matter, even if you hold the copyright.

questions.prompt: Software whose source code is available for anyone to see, change and share (under its licence) is called:
questions.explanation: Examples include Linux, LibreOffice and Mozilla Firefox.

questions.prompt: Which of these is usually proprietary software?
questions.explanation: Proprietary software is owned by a company which keeps the source code private and controls how it is used.

questions.prompt: What usually happens to proprietary software if you copy and share it with friends without permission?

expected_answer.value: It breaks the licence and may be illegal

options: It breaks the licence and may be illegal
questions.explanation: A licence lists what you may do. Unauthorised copying (piracy) breaks it.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct?

expected_answer.value: Open source does not always mean free of cost

options: Open source software cannot be used by companies
Open source does not always mean free of cost
All free software is open source
Open source means the code is secret
questions.explanation: Open source is about access to the code and freedom to change it. Some open-source products are sold with support or services.

questions.prompt: Presenting someone else's work as your own without giving credit is called:
questions.explanation: Plagiarism is a form of dishonesty and can break copyright law.

questions.prompt: Which is the honest way to use a paragraph from a website in your project?

expected_answer.value: Put it in quotation marks and name the source

options: Put it in quotation marks and name the source
Copy it and delete the website name
Change two words and claim it as yours
questions.explanation: Quoting with credit, or paraphrasing with credit, avoids plagiarism.

questions.prompt: Which of these is protected by copyright?

expected_answer.value: A song you can hear online

options: The idea of writing a song, with nothing written down
A song you can hear online
The name of a day, such as Monday
questions.explanation: Copyright protects the original expression of a work (the song itself), not bare ideas or common facts.

questions.prompt: Why are Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) given to creators?

expected_answer.value: So creators can control and benefit from their original work

options: So that nobody can read the work
So that the work is always free
So that only companies can create
So creators can control and benefit from their original work
questions.explanation: IPR encourage people to create by giving them legal protection over their work.

questions.prompt: Which sign in the browser suggests that a website connection is secure?

expected_answer.value: A padlock with https in the address

options: A padlock with https in the address
questions.explanation: HTTPS and the padlock show that the connection is encrypted. It does not prove the shop itself is honest.

questions.prompt: You get a call asking for the OTP of your card "to cancel a wrong payment". What should you do?

expected_answer.value: Never share it; hang up and contact the bank through its official number

options: Never share it; hang up and contact the bank through its official number
Share it only if the caller sounds polite
questions.explanation: Banks never ask for OTPs. Sharing it lets a fraudster complete a payment.

questions.prompt: Tricking people into giving passwords or card details through a fake message or website is called:
questions.explanation: Phishing messages look genuine; check the sender and web address before clicking.

questions.prompt: Why is data converted into a coded form (encryption) when you pay online?

expected_answer.value: So that anyone who intercepts it cannot read it

options: So that it uses less electricity
So that the page loads in colour
So that anyone who intercepts it cannot read it
So that the shop can sell it
questions.explanation: Encryption protects card and personal details while travelling over the network.
